## Schema selection terminology

Schema holds Field roots and metadata; its equality ignores schema metadata, while configurable comparison can include it. Projectable exposes a borrowed Schema, and Projection selects field IDs plus four metadata-column flags and a blob policy. These are in-memory schemas/selections, not executed read plans. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:24-31; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:174-177; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1099-1108; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1191-1204)

Field paths use backticks/doubled backticks; minimal path formatting quotes literal dots/backticks, while expression-oriented formatting quotes other punctuation too. See the [schema API supplement](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-schema.md) for edge cases, validation and exact signatures. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:1567-1735)

## Cache serialization vocabulary

LCE1 envelope carries a type identity and body version; CacheDecode distinguishes Hit from a reasoned Miss. CacheEntryWriter/Reader manage typed-body sections and absolute offsets, independently of the16-byte key digest. See [cache module](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md) and [format reconstruction](L3-symbols/format-spec.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/codec.rs:144-228; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:28-38; rust/lance-core/src/cache/entry_io.rs:117-126)


## Weighted cache budgets

Moka and Quick are in-memory CacheBackend implementations. Their eviction weights include fixed key cost plus declared entry size; shared-buffer-aware deep traversal is a separate callback-based metric. Quick can partition a budget among shards or use a single shard, so fitting the total cache does not imply admission to one shard. (rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:25-47; rust/lance-core/src/cache/moka.rs:186-199; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:40-50; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:101-106; rust/lance-core/src/cache/quick.rs:216-229)


## Typed cache handles

LanceCache clones and child namespaces share backend, counters and type-aware memory callbacks. WeakLanceCache preserves namespace without a strong state reference and can compute a sized value after expiry without caching it. CacheStats counts successful coalesced loads as hits and excludes loader errors; these semantics differ from a raw request success/failure counter. [Full cache surface](L1-modules/rust-lance-core-cache.md). (rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:212-263; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:314-358; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:420-471; rust/lance-core/src/cache/mod.rs:570-659)

## Encoded row identity and operation disposition

InlineRowIds keeps byte content and a shared lazy digest memo together so clones reuse both and replacing the wrapper does not carry an old digest into new bytes. Its digest identifies encoded content, not decoded-row equivalence. RowIdMeta chooses inline bytes or hidden-column storage. (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:27-98; rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:141-166)

The format-layer Transaction is a public protobuf wrapper; its schema-change classification is a conservative operation disposition used to decide where validation may be needed, not validation itself. It has no commit lifecycle in its local body. (rust/lance-table/src/format/transaction.rs:16-82)


## Three version domains and manifest ownership

Dataset version is Manifest.version (with bit63 identifying a detached version), writer version is library-specific semver metadata, and data storage version is an exact ConcreteFileVersion. Treat these as separate domains. A Manifest is an in-memory snapshot with shared fragments and private cached logical offsets; its protobuf serialization is not a complete file or a commit. (rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:39-128; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:547-557; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:702-748)

Fragment metadata ties columns of the same physical rows to base DataFiles, ordered overlays, optional deletion and inline/column lineage. Every-file operations must account for overlays; lineage lookup intentionally uses base files only. These metadata rules now connect the flag policy to manifest decoding and shallow cloning; dataset IO and transaction publication are still untraced. (rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:519-558; rust/lance-table/src/format/fragment.rs:589-725; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:242-313; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1011-1045)


## Three distinct coverage domains

Index fragment_bitmap tracks fragment IDs; overlay bitmaps track physical offsets within a fragment; key-existence Bloom data tracks encoded join keys for conflict detection. They cannot substitute for one another. Unknown index coverage is None, sparse overlay coverage is positional per field, and a Bloom overlap is only a possible key conflict. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:62-67; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay.rs:65-74; rust/lance-table/src/format/key_existence.rs:175-212)

Covered index fields are dependencies whose values are carried with results; keyed fields decide which search the index can answer. Physical metadata currently validates a suffix representation. The protobuf's future independent-covering feature must not be assumed implemented by that validator. (rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:36-51; rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs:160-247; rust/lance-table/src/feature_flags.rs:86-97)


## File-version request, identity and footer

Caller Stable/Next selectors resolve to exact2.2/2.3 in this snapshot. Persisted identities have no ordering; use explicit capabilities instead of comparing release numbers. V2.0 standard footer is(0,3), embedded footer and DataFile metadata are(2,0), while manifest string is2.0. These spellings describe the same exact identity. Footer-only detection reads8 bytes and does not certify a valid complete file. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60)

Overlay staleness is a metadata-derived conservative exclusion set: union newer changes to indexed dependency fields or their ancestors/descendants, then consumers must re-evaluate affected rows. This differs from resolving the newest value and from deleting rows; the helper only returns/accumulates physical offset sets. (rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:4-13; rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:35-158)


## Positional lineage glossary

- **RowDatasetVersionRun / Sequence:** one dataset version per positional span, stored as runs aligned with row-ID order. Numeric span coordinates are not stable row IDs; consumers use cumulative lengths. [Version module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:44-80; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:272-311)
- **SpilledRowLineage:** preloaded row IDs/creation/update sequences keyed by fragment ID, allowing synchronous manifest preparation to preserve column-stored lineage. Loading itself remains a caller responsibility. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:25-42; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/version.rs:750-769)
- **HoleRuns:** maximal missing-offset runs plus present-count prefixes, supporting offset-to-ordinal rank and inverse selection. It represents holes in a row-ID segment, not dataset-version runs or deletion-file IO. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:4-34; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/runs.rs:132-190)


## Row-ID representation terms

- **Bitmap:** internal presence bits indexed LSB first within each byte; logical length is separate from byte capacity. Constructors normalize padding, raw construction does not. The schema comment disagrees on bit order. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/bitmap.rs:7-105; protos/rowids.proto:51-58)
- **EncodedU64Array:** owned U16/U32 relative offsets plus a base or plain U64 values; compressed does not imply sorted. Wire packed integers are little-endian. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/encoded_array.rs:8-26; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:174-230)
- **Range folding:** decoder merges adjacency and groups ascending separated ranges through the segment helper; sequence writer expands the compact Ranges form back into plain wire Range arms. This changes in-memory representation without adding a protobuf arm. [Codec overview](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:60-96; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:232-255; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:376-398)


## Segment coordinates and scan state

- **U64Segment:** one of six in-memory representations of an intended distinct u64 sequence. Numeric values, present ordinals and enclosing numeric bounds are separate coordinates. Selection chooses five forms; compact Ranges comes from explicit range grouping/bitmap conversion. [Module](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:16-82; rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:196-299)
- **SegmentCursor / SegmentCursorState:** a public borrowed segment reader and its crate-visible bitmap byte/rank state. The wrapper fixes the source; reusable state alone does not. Dense expansion batches contiguous set-bit runs, while selection indices count present values. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:749-954)


## Row-ID sequences and ordinal selection

RowIdSequence preserves fragment row order across segments. Stable numeric IDs, ordinal positions and tree-map set membership are distinct: set conversion discards order, while masks translate selected IDs back into ordinal ranges. Public checked construction rejects duplicates within one input; raw range/slice conversions and extend do not enforce table-wide uniqueness. [Sequence analysis](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs.md). (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:39-52; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:209-265; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:302-319; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:609-797; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:865-905)

RowIdSeqSlice is a borrowed positional view. RowIdSequenceCursor instead owns scan counters without a source lifetime: it rewinds for decreasing requests and resets segment state at boundaries, but callers must keep its sequence stable across calls. Internal selection clips at EOF; the public ReadBatchParams adapter has separate bounds/error behavior. (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:54-170; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:456-494; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:559-592; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:908-943; rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:1055-1127)



## Creation lineage during transaction preparation

Creation version records first appearance; last-update version records the commit changing values. The reviewed transaction helper resolves stable IDs back to source physical offsets, preserves known creation versions, falls back to1 for unavailable creation of a found source, and stamps new IDs with the supplied commit version. Writer-placed lineage means row-ID Column or creation-version Column; it is a metadata predicate, not a provenance check. [Table details](L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) and [local scenario](L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) separate these synchronous metadata mutations from the separately documented [IO](L3-symbols/protocol-io.md) and [publication](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md) protocols. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:21-79; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/row_version.rs:258-295)




## Transaction intent and one-attempt preparation

A Transaction stores read_version,UUID,Operation,optional tag and shared string properties. An Operation names one of16 change kinds with typed payloads. PreparedIndices separately carries current-attempt original/prepared index metadata and fragment-reuse intent; it is not persisted by these containers. Retry/conflict/publication behavior is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). [Transaction API](L1-modules/rust-lance-table-transactions.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/builder.rs:12-25; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:37-262; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:4-18; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/prepare.rs:44-100)

CoverageIdentity means UUID plus optional fragment bitmap, with other index metadata excluded from equality. ReadVersionState means borrowed manifest/index evidence from a transaction's fixed read version; it carries no runtime check that the pair matches. UpdatedFragmentOffsets means per-fragment physical offset bitmaps for partial column-update lineage. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction.rs:62-102; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:277-282)




## Equality versus conflict compatibility

Operation equality compares represented intent; different operation kinds always differ. Separate metadata predicates compare config upserts/deletes or table/schema/field metadata scopes. Their bool results are consumed by the commit conflict resolver, whose directional matrix is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). Durable commit-outcome identity uses protobuf forms in the inspected path, not these in-memory payload comparisons. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:18-29; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/conflicts.rs:863-991; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2225-2238; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:257-297)




## Operation pre-validation

Pre-validation checks operation shape against an optional current manifest. It is synchronous metadata inspection with no storage IO; its success does not certify physical files, schema completeness in modern formats or transaction compatibility. Merge field-binding protection and a separate base-file rewrite detector serve different purposes: binding safety versus latest-version stamping. (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:18-200; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/validate.rs:301-462; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs:1196-1255)




## Durable transaction representation

Operation intent converts to a generated protobuf transaction before storage. Rust optional-empty states and transient rewrite metadata may disappear; unknown update-mode values decode as row rewrite, and empty rewrite groups take a legacy fallback. Therefore in-memory equality, decoded operation equality and persisted protobuf identity are distinct contracts. Byte storage/outcome recovery is in [the commit protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:151-184; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:244-283; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:408-422; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/proto.rs:555-569; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:257-297)




## Stored index provenance versus live coverage

An index segment's stored fragment bitmap can name retired source fragments, while history maps their rows to later destinations. Unknown coverage (None), known empty coverage and known retired provenance have different retention behavior. TaggedLineage separates stored coverage membership from whether history is walkable; known-empty destination lists differ from unknown lineage. These distinctions drive invalidation and retention, with implementation navigation in the [index protocol](L3-symbols/protocol-index.md). (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/index_maintenance.rs:219-348; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/index_maintenance.rs:524-632; rust/lance-table/src/system_index/frag_reuse/lineage.rs:23-140)




## Tagged format state and operation admission

A sticky manifest reader flag can keep the tagged format contract active after the entry is removed. Entry recognition, format recognition, paired-flag validation and operation admission are separate predicates: an Untagged admission does not imply the sticky bit is absent. MovesNoRows is also a reason name, while its admitted operations include in-place column rewrites. Use the exact gate branches for development decisions. ## Decoder facade glossary

Scheduling selects byte ranges and produces page messages; decoding materializes Arrow arrays through tasks. Array and structural message grammars are distinct. A ReadBatchTask carries a future plus expected row count. Structural byte targets adapt using reported decoded size and can overshoot; array i32-offset limits are a separate mechanism. RequestBatch aggregates I/O calls while preserving each caller's buffer order. [Module contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1542-1558; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:1636-1734; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2089-2199; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:2863-3064)


## Primitive index and value terms

A mini-block has distinct byte, top-level-row and leaf-value coordinates. A trailer begins a row continued in the next block; that next block has a preamble. Constant pages retain one scalar plus repetition/definition levels, then materialize selected leaf positions. Dictionary normalization moves null dictionary entries into key validity before encoding; physical null-key repair prevents invalid hidden indices when validity is removed. [Helper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/chunk_index.rs:185-343; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/constant.rs:341-492; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/dict.rs:30-170)


## Blob decode view and representation

Original BlobLayout stores position/size descriptions plus same-file payload buffers; descriptor-only reads and binary materialization use separate cache views. Blob-v2 prepared records become kind/position/size/blob_id/blob_uri descriptors, with sidecar/URI handling outside this encoder. A payload shard is a byte-targeted group of original Blob reads, distinct from dataset fragments or MemWAL shards;32MiB is a target that can be exceeded. [Blob contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). ## Fixed slots and map entries

A fixed-size-list dimension gives the number of child slots per outer row. Null outer rows still reserve those slots; variable-size descendants under them can be cleared with a garbage mask. Map entries are Struct key/value rows whose offsets and parent validity are reconstructed through rep/def layers. The current complex FSL path requires immediate Struct children, while Map requires unsorted entries and a nonnullable key. [Nested wrapper contracts](L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md). # Lance engine orientation

> Refresh 2026-10-07, `84d1681e07af565837f2d97e72ff1b8b040cd15c`: source coordinates updated. [Changed contracts](L3-symbols/refresh-2026-10-07.md) supersede pre-refresh claims only for the listed changes. Unchanged analysis is retained.

**Navigation and contracts; source access is expected.** Start here, choose a path, and open its ordered source set. Deep format details live in the [format contract](L3-symbols/format-spec.md), terminology in the [engine glossary](L0-glossary.md), and exact retained declarations in the [frozen symbol snapshot](L3-symbols/symbol-index.md). [Scope and trust](V21-PROTOCOL.md).

## Architecture and state ownership

Lance presents a versioned Dataset over immutable data files and versioned metadata. A fragment groups physical columns for the same rows; its manifest entry carries deletion, overlay and lineage metadata. A Dataset handle owns a manifest snapshot plus stores, commit handler and session/cache handles. Publishing a new manifest makes a mutation visible; finishing a data file alone does not publish a dataset. (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:8-87; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-572; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:1-264)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  API[Dataset / Scanner / write and index builders] --> Plan[Scan planning and execution nodes]
  API --> Tx[Transaction preparation and commit]
  Plan --> Index[Scalar / vector / full-text indices]
  Plan --> Fragment[Fragment reads and row identity]
  Fragment --> File[lance-file exact-version readers]
  API --> Writer[Fragment / file writers]
  Writer --> File
  File --> Encoding[lance-encoding page and buffer mechanisms]
  File --> IO[lance-io stores and scheduled reads]
  Tx --> Table[lance-table manifests, operations and conflicts]
  Table --> Publish[CommitHandler publication]
  Publish --> IO
  Index --> IO
  Core[lance-core schemas, errors and common data structures] --> API
  Core --> Table
  Protos[Handwritten protobuf schemas] --> Table
  Protos --> File
```

The arrows identify ownership/call boundaries rather than a claim that every request crosses every box. Scanner creates a physical plan; the DataFusion adapter executes it and returns a RecordBatch stream. Encoding describes pages and schedules their bytes through an I/O seam; it does not commit Dataset versions. Index creation writes index state before committing CreateIndex metadata. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2653-2669; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-134; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:688-735)

## Read path

**Entry:** `dataset.scan().try_into_stream().await?`. The stream must be consumed to execute reads. This is a trace of the public Rust path; it is not a command that was run during KB work.

1. `Dataset::scan` clones the snapshot into `Scanner`. Configure projection/filter/vector/limit before planning. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704)
2. `Scanner::create_plan_impl` validates options, resolves full-text/query filters, chooses vector, full-text, MinHash or filtered read source, and adds filtering, ordering, limit and final projection. Scalar index use is conditioned on prefiltering or absence of nearest search. Conflicting search modes error. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3246-3411)
3. `try_into_stream` passes the plan, batch size and statistics callback to `execute_plan`. Multiple output partitions are merged with order preservation when ordering exists; execution starts at partition 0 of that final plan. (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2653-2669; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)
4. The selected source reads fragment metadata/deletions/lineage and reaches exact-version file readers. File open loads footer/global/column metadata; prepared reads schedule pages, decode selected values and materialize batches. The local contract is in the [frozen shared-reader record](L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs.md); source ranges are rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028. No guarantee is made that every query reads every column or uses an index.

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2653-2696,3246-3411` → `rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761` → `rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028`. For a particular scan operator, follow the scanner's selected source rather than opening all execution nodes.

## Write path

**Entry:** `Dataset::write(reader, destination, Some(params)).await?`.

1. `Dataset::write` constructs `InsertBuilder`, applies params and calls `execute_stream`; the input reader is converted into stream/schema. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-120)
2. Resolve destination/store/version, validate the write, resolve target bases and write fragments. A fixed data filename combined with target bases is rejected. `execute_uncommitted` stops after building a transaction: data objects may exist, but no manifest has been published. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:144-265)
3. Create and overwrite produce `Operation::Overwrite`; append produces `Operation::Append`. The transaction's read version comes from the destination snapshot or 0 for a new destination. File assembly/flush belongs to the fragment writer, and its exact bytes to the selected file-version writer. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:267-315; rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1733-1839)
4. `do_commit` configures `CommitBuilder`. Existing datasets use the retrying transaction path (or the explicitly selected detached path); new datasets use `commit_new_dataset`. Detached new-dataset creation is rejected; detached commit cannot use V1 manifest naming. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:148-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)
5. Successful publication returns a Dataset carrying the committed manifest/location and caches. Data-file existence is not commit evidence; error/outcome recovery belongs to `io/commit.rs`. (rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:516-572; rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:269-297)

**Ordered initial read set (5 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-315` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1733-1839` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-572` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1649-1869`. The exact persisted manifest contract is already available through the [frozen table I/O record](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs.md).

## Compaction path

**Entry:** `compact_files(&mut dataset, options, remap_options).await?`.

1. Construct and run the compaction planner. Reject eager index remapping on a tagged fragment-reuse history. No planned tasks means no new committed version. Execute planned rewrites with bounded concurrency and collect successful results. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152)
2. Each rewrite validates its target exact file version, refreshes required fragment statistics and chooses binary-copy or scan/re-encode. A forced binary-copy request cannot silently fall back. Capture old physical row addresses only when a consumer needs remapping; stable row IDs use their own lineage. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2494-2569; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:2693-2789)
3. `commit_compaction` validates tagged-history/remap requirements and takes the **minimum RewriteResult.read_version**, so conflicts since task planning remain visible even if the caller opened a newer Dataset handle. Address-style outputs reserve fragment IDs; remap indices now or produce deferred fragment-reuse metadata according to the selected protocol. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3227-3337)
4. Commit a Rewrite operation through Dataset's normal commit boundary. Old files are not made safe to delete merely by writing replacements; retain manifest/version retention policy. (rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3662-3693; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:74-123)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1028-1152,2494-2789,3227-3337,3662-3693` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1649-1869` → `rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1424-1691,2851-3107` → [frozen manifest application](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/transaction/manifest_build.rs.md). Split copy mechanics or a specific index remapper into a separate task instead of expanding this read set without bound.

## Index build and query path

**Entry:** `DatasetIndexExt::create_index` / `create_index_builder`; query through Scanner.

1. The Dataset extension constructs `CreateIndexBuilder`; optional name and replace settings are applied before awaiting it. The builder validates one-column admission and reserves names against all stored indices, including unsupported ones. (rust/lance/src/index.rs:2053-2087; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210)
2. Build/train through the selected scalar/vector index implementation; `execute_uncommitted` yields metadata without publication. Multi-segment FM-Index construction has a separate atomic multi-index path. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210; rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:688-705)
3. On replacement, collect same-name metadata to remove, then commit CreateIndex with newly built metadata. Reload the committed index by UUID so the return value reflects commit-time changes; missing UUID after commit errors. (rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:698-735)
4. Scanner later selects index-backed or scan-backed sources from query/filter options. Data not covered by an index must be accounted for by that query path; never equate a stored index bitmap with all current rows. The distinctions are in the [frozen index metadata contract](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). (rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3326-3411)

**Ordered initial read set (4 files):** `rust/lance/src/index.rs:2053-2087` → `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-210,688-735` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3326-3411` → [frozen index metadata](L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/format/index.rs.md). Concrete scalar/IVF-PQ implementation choices belong to the M2 index Module Map, not an assumed universal build pipeline.

## Essential distinctions

- File format version, Dataset manifest version, per-row creation/update version and index version are different domains. Never compare them interchangeably. [Exact version matrix](L3-symbols/format-spec.md); [glossary](L0-glossary.md).
- Stable logical row IDs differ from physical `(fragment_id, offset)` addresses; compaction changes physical addresses. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:6-79; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:34-81)
- Declaration in a protobuf union does not establish acceptance in every exact file version. Reader grammar and writer selection are independent checks. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:93-110; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:93-118)
- Stable format compatibility is durable; unstable formats may change; frozen legacy paths are not new-feature extension points. (AGENTS.md:5-20)

This orientation completes M1's architecture and four public paths. Detailed subsystem/API contracts and navigation tests remain independently tracked in M2–M4; no build or runtime execution is claimed.

## Development entry

Choose a task in the [ordered navigation index](L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md), then read its contract and bounded implementation set. API-only questions start at [public contracts and bindings](L3-symbols/public-api.md).

## Ownership and opening

FileReader shares its Reader, Metadata, ordinary PageTable and optional statistics PageTable through Arcs, while owning the supplied Schema. Clone retains shared underlying dictionary arrays through Schema's Clone behavior. object_reader is public and can be replaced without refreshing stored metadata. fragment_id is retained for Debug; this file does not generate row IDs. There is no custom Drop or shutdown protocol. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:41-66)

~~~text
try_new(store, path, supplied_schema)
`-- try_new_with_fragment_id(fragment=0, min=0, max=schema.max_id, cache=None)
    |-- ObjectStore.open
    |-- read_metadata
    `-- try_new_from_reader(metadata=Some)
        |-- ordinary PageTable load/cache using supplied path and bounds
        `-- statistics PageTable load/cache using Reader.path/stats
            `-- read_metadata again unless cache serves it
~~~

The two table futures are polled concurrently with try_join. Supplied metadata is trusted for ordinary-table loading; the statistics loader independently obtains metadata from the reader. Without a cache, ordinary construction reads metadata twice. The separate path, reader path, metadata, schema and field bounds are not reconciled. An error returns before construction; no rollback or explicit abort guard is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:139-208; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-294)

Every constructor here requires Schema. It neither discovers schema nor hydrates dictionary values, despite stale documentation about an optional manifest. Self-describing opening is a separate table-layer trait: it reads Metadata, requires manifest_position, reads Manifest, populates schema dictionaries, then calls try_new_from_reader. Dataset fragment opening supplies its schema and file field bounds; the full Dataset wrapper remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:126-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1154-1210; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:1374-1401)

## Cache and metadata contract

The private typed string key has stable schema `lance.file.previous.string-key`, version 1, and writes one string. Stable value IDs are `lance.file.previous.Metadata`, `lance.file.previous.PageTable` and `lance.file.previous.OptionalPageTable`; compiler type names are diagnostic only. The key contains no explicit schema, field bounds, fragment ID, object-store identity, ETag or file version. The supplied LanceCache may add a namespace; this local adapter adds no invalidation or persistent codec. Cached statistics absence is an Option value. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:68-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:181-198; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-288)

A cache miss reads the last min(file_size, block_size) bytes, extracts the eight-byte metadata position at footer[-16..-8], and either fetches the earlier framed struct or decodes its tail slice. That helper checks at least 16 tail bytes but does not check magic/version. Tail-position arithmetic and in-buffer framing do not locally guard malformed offsets/lengths; they can panic before decoding returns an error. Do not infer current-reader footer validation from this V1 path. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:210-234; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263)

Statistics opening loads one batch covering field IDs 0 through max(leaf_field_ids), panicking on an empty leaf-ID list. page_stats_schema matches requested data IDs against parsed statistics root names, then projects their IDs and immediate children. It retains schema order and can return Some(empty). read_page_stats returns None for absent table or empty projection; otherwise reads batch 0. A disagreement between caller metadata and the independently loaded statistics table can reach an unwrap. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-267; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:398-445)

## Read APIs and scheduling

The method and free read_batch use the explicit per-call schema, rather than the stored reader schema promised by the method comment. Empty projection returns InvalidInput; the free-function comment about a with_row_id flag and panic is obsolete. No upfront subset/type validation occurs. Root fields are read with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), and RecordBatch construction performs the final assembled-array check. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:324-335; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:485-507)

read_range immediately accepts any empty/reversed range as an empty batch, even beyond the end. Otherwise metadata splits across batches; reads are ordered and all results are retained. A single result is cloned; multiple results are concatenated in spawn_blocking. take first uses metadata grouping, which copies and sorts input, preserving duplicates but losing original order. It checks grouped batch IDs afterward, and its secondary offset check compares against whole-file length rather than batch length. Both APIs materialize the complete result; no local abort-on-drop mechanism is provided for blocking concat. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-194)

batches_stream lazily filters ascending batch IDs and requests complete batches with fixed outer concurrency 2. It owns reader/projection through Arcs and advertises the supplied Arrow schema. Inner field reads retain their own Reader parallelism. This function does not spawn a Tokio task; a separately inspected Dataset ranges_to_tasks wrapper does spawn per-range tasks. Do not merge their cancellation or scheduling contracts. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:448-483; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:158-186)

## Recursive reconstruction and edge cases

read_array dispatches by reconstructed DataType, not field.encoding: fixed stride first, then Null, the four byte-array types, Struct, Dictionary and the two variable-list widths. Unsupported types reach unimplemented. Every FSL enters fixed-stride dispatch regardless of its child; Interval has a width helper but is absent from that predicate. get_page_info reports missing field/batch entries as InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:509-576; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181)

| Type/path | Local reconstruction | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed stride | Page position/length and selector go to plain codec | No field-nullability bitmap passed |
| Binary/string | Same, plus field.nullable | Equal offsets become null only when nullable |
| Dictionary | Plain keys plus cloned loaded values Arc | Missing dictionary/values unwraps |
| Struct | Sequential recursive child reads | No parent page/validity restored |
| Null | Synthesize count, no payload IO | End/max checks differ from plain; reversed range can underflow; Ranges panics |
| List/LargeList | Read offsets, read child values, normalize and build | Parent validity absent; reconstructed child is item/nullable=true |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:559-808; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229.

List range offsets include the terminal endpoint. Direct empty Indices accesses first/last and panics; public empty FileReader.take avoids per-column reads because grouping yields no groups. List Indices reads the whole first-to-last offset span, then sequentially reads each selected child range and concatenates; duplicates repeat those reads. Its offset lookup uses reader.page_table even when the function received another table, while child recursion uses that argument. Null selector validity is ignored on list and Null paths. Sortedness, arithmetic, child existence and offset coherence are caller/file assumptions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:370-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:578-623; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-807)

The list constructor chooses a child field named item with nullable=true from actual child data type. It does not preserve arbitrary child metadata/name/nullability or parent nullness. Struct reconstruction similarly supplies no parent validity. These are frozen representation and reconstruction limits, not promises made by current-format readers. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:671-686; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:724-738; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:795-807; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Twelve active tests pin stable cache discriminator strings; seven-row multi-batch numeric/string/dictionary take; nullable empty-string conversion; combined-input struct/list roundtrip; one-row struct/list slice; Null lengths and weak is_err boundaries; List/LargeList take; sliced list equality plus file size<1000; one-batch numeric range; even-batch stream order; Boolean take with 256-byte blocks; and a narrow file opened under a wider schema with explicit field bounds. They do not prove malformed-file safety, cache invalidation, cancellation, parent-null preservation, arbitrary selectors or full multi-fragment behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:827-1562)

The Boolean test is active reader-level coverage: 5,000 modulo-5 bits, indices [2,4,5,8,4555], expected [false,false,true,false,true]. It supplements the commented-out codec-local test and does not assert actual IO request counts. The projection test writes only f50 from a 100-field schema, then opens with full schema but min=max=f50; it does not test projection from a physically 100-column file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:1459-1561)

Dependencies provide Arrow arrays/arithmetic/concat, borrowed async Reader/ObjectStore IO, Lance typed cache and metadata framing, tracing and boxed recursion/ordered futures. There is no local environment variable, Cargo feature, runtime registry, mutable global, unsafe block, durability commit or writer lifecycle. The generic offset type and private cache trait adapt existing implementations; they are not new-format plugin seams. Preserve historical behavior unless legacy repair is explicitly in scope. ## Manifest read lifecycle

read_manifest trusts optional size or HEADs for it, requests last64KiB, retries once without known size only after successful bytes fail minimum16/magic checks, then uses signed LE footer offset as usize. It does not inspect footer version bytes or invoke feature capability gates. Bounds arithmetic is unchecked: malformed offsets or a trimmed body too short for prefix+footer can panic via arithmetic/slices. Length mismatch after trimming is InvalidInput; short-tail/wrong-magic and slow-path minimum20 are CorruptFile(path). GET errors and decode errors do not trigger cached-size retry. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:32-128)

For a larger body it opens a sized reader and accumulates16MiB chunks in file order under bounded concurrency, appends tail and decodes through ChunkedBuf without one full concatenation. All body chunks are retained before Prost decoding, so this is not bounded-memory streaming parsing. Within-chunk Bytes fields can share backing; cross-boundary copy_to_bytes allocates. After conversion detach_sparse_inline_row_ids copies nonzero inline total when less than one quarter of recorded message length, reducing retained backing at a transient copy cost. Performance numbers in source comments are not measurements here. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:75-127; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:19-159; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:396-424)

read_manifest_indexes has a different retry: only a known size plus exact error-text substring file size is too small causes a second read without hint. Missing index_section returns empty without IO. It converts every metadata entry but does not verify uniqueness or dataset feature compatibility. Private read_index_section opens the selected view and invokes length-prefixed generic read_message. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:129-175; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:161-199)

## Manifest write lifecycle

V1 default format first writes schema dictionaries; exact V2 variants skip that step. do_write_manifest writes Some index vector even if empty, or clears inherited offset for None; then does the same for optional inline transaction; finally writes manifest. Successful earlier writes and offset mutations are not rolled back by later error/cancellation. The returned position is where the manifest length prefix begins. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:177-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:53-63; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:84-92)

Contextual canonical writer creates ObjectWriter, calls this body writer, appends footer via WriteExt, shuts down and only then logs create. It uses lance-file footer constants0/2/LANC, whereas table format facade declares0/1/LANC; read_manifest checks neither pair. Commit handler selection and local publication are now covered in the [commit supplement](rust-lance-table-commit.md). ManifestDescribing is a legacy V1 schema-only provider and directly calls do_write_manifest on a fresh V1 envelope. (rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:31-40; rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:199-230; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:95-107; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33; rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:51-56; rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-251)

## Deletion path and representation

Paths combine supplied base with _deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{random_id}.arrow or .bin. base_id is ignored locally; caller must select directory/store. NoDeletions returns None; explicit Set(empty) and Bitmap(empty) still write. Representation is chosen by enum arm, not density at IO time. Set serialization uses unspecified HashSet order and a single Arrow IPC ZSTD batch with nonnullable row_id:UInt32. Bitmap serializes Roaring as-is with no explicit run optimization. Every payload is built in Vec before one put. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-134)

Array reader loads full object and all batches before checking exactly one batch and exact schema equality. It deduplicates offsets into HashSet, rejects nulls, and returns Set without normalization. Bitmap reader wraps Roaring errors with path and returns Bitmap. Neither validates physical bounds or num_deleted_rows, resolves base_id, or explicitly checks trailing bytes after Roaring decode. A malformed Arrow iterator error becomes CorruptFile(path), while constructor error uses generic conversion. Guarded unwraps rely on count/schema checks. (rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:135-216)

Contextual dataset reader resolves directory before cache lookup, uses DeletionFileKey, and on miss resolves store, reads and inserts Arc vector. It is get-then-read-then-insert, with no explicit single-flight in that wrapper. Fragment write_deletions drops a fully deleted fragment; when count>=physical but coverage differs it errors; otherwise writes metadata. That count-conditional check does not locally reject every out-of-range offset in a smaller set. These callers are contextual and remain pending whole-file analysis. (rust/lance/src/io/deletion.rs:11-43; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:3005-3036)

## Dependencies, extensibility and verification limits

Manifest depends on ObjectStore/Writer/CommitHandler location metadata, Prost and table codecs; chunk concurrency follows Reader::io_parallelism with minimum1. Deletion depends on Arrow IPC ZSTD and Roaring formats, core DeletionVector and audit tracing. Object-store implementations and Writer trait are storage extension boundaries; neither reviewed file declares environment settings or an index/encoding registry. Legacy ManifestProvider adapts the old writer and remains frozen compatibility scope. ## Alignment and shared future lifecycle

MergeStream keeps one pending chunk from each input. It emits the minimum remaining count, splitting bigger chunks with shared futures and Arrow slices. A whole unsplit task moves its original future directly. Split errors become Wrapped with the original Error reachable through SharedReadError::source. Input task order determines column merge order; FuturesOrdered yields component results in that order. Any input stream ending stops the merge without checking remaining totals. The outer stream does not await batch data; emitted futures perform the actual merge. Dropping one split future does not itself invalidate another shared handle, and retained slices can retain the whole source batch. Declared sizes must match actual data or slicing can panic; equal actual lengths are checked by RecordBatchExt::merge. Matching field names are not simple concatenation: nested structures may merge and other conflicts keep the left column. Left schema metadata survives. Certain nested-list merge branches can panic; those dependency internals are only contextually read, not fully analyzed. Metadata Results are captured in those futures: an input batch error propagates first and can mask a precomputed metadata error. Chunks are aligned to whole batches, capped by selected rows left; a larger task can exceed the target. A nonfinal size change permanently disables both fast paths after draining any usable cached ID chunk. Zero-size tasks do not alter the inferred size; a different final size is allowed. Selection offsets count rows in the requested selection, while ranges/indices identify physical positions in the sequence. Helpers slice params then often unwrap Results, so invalid selection can panic despite a Result-returning public transformer. base_tokenizer optional string=1 identifies concrete lexical tokenizer after document extraction; analyzer profiles expand into it plus concrete options before persistence. `copy_blob_columns` is crate-internal deep-clone support. Commit clone invokes it before publishing a managed-blob target. ## Data flow and invariants

1. Construct a target Dataset view using the target store/base/URI, refreshed manifest and empty base-store cache. Enumerate and deduplicate managed `(Option<base ID>, URI)` references. A local managed reference copies to the same relative path; an explicit-base reference copies to a fresh `_blobs/<uuid>.blob` path. Copy payload objects before rewriting descriptors. Errors propagate to clone orchestration. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:215-259`.
2. `replace_array` recursively rebuilds struct/list/large-list containers while preserving nulls. For copied explicit references it emits local Managed descriptors, nulls the base-ID slot and changes the URI; position and size remain intact. Unmatched descriptors remain unchanged. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:30-128`.
3. `rewrite_blob_columns` returns immediately if no replacements/blob fields exist. Otherwise it projects blob-bearing top-level columns and row addresses per fragment, prepares a preserving BlobV2 rewrite plan, and writes updated arrays through the fragment updater. Replaced file fields are tombstoned with -2; empty data files are removed. Fragment identity and unrelated file columns survive. `rust/lance/src/dataset/blob/clone.rs:132-213`.

Keep `(base, URI)` identity distinct even when URI strings match across bases. Preserve descriptor offsets/sizes and container null layout.   520 | /// Called from the final data-changing merge-insert commit for a compaction
``````text
  521 | /// target, so the rows and the generation that describes them publish
  522 | /// together.
  523 | ///
  524 | /// A proposed generation must be **strictly greater** than the one the latest
  525 | /// state records for that shard, and a stale one fails the whole transaction.
  526 | /// Accepting it while keeping the larger marker would publish that worker's row
  527 | /// mutations under a generation it did not produce, and anything reading only
  528 | /// the marker could then stop serving SSTables whose rows were never inserted.
  529 | ///

  532 |     indices: &mut [IndexMetadata],
  533 |     dataset_version: u64,
``````

## SharedStream state transitions

The queue belongs to whichever side lags; the other side must have zero buffered count. A bounded permit is forgotten when a clone is enqueued and restored when that clone is consumed or discarded on dead-side drop. Polling upstream happens with the mutex released, but ownership prevents the peer from polling concurrently. Ready clears ownership; Pending keeps it. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:28-45; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:82-247)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Owned: obtain permit and claim side
    Owned --> Owned: upstream Pending
    Owned --> Idle: item ready; clone for live peer
    Owned --> Exhausted: upstream None
    Owned --> Idle: owning handle dropped
    Exhausted --> Exhausted: drain own buffer, then repeat None
```

This diagram omits per-side queue and permit substates; the transition implementation and ordering are given above, including capacity acquisition before poll-owner arbitration. Bounded(0) cannot reach Owned; upstream panic can remove inner without restoration; clone panic poisons the mutex. These are not recoverable states implemented by the diagram. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:47-80; rust/lance-core/src/utils/futures.rs:127-247)

## CPU runtime publication and child reset

The first caller sets the installation-election flag, optionally registers the child hook, allocates/leaks a Runtime, then publishes its pointer. Other callers yield until non-null publication. The pointer lifetime comments justify unsafe shared references because allocation is never reclaimed; SeqCst is used throughout publication/reset. Child reset clears pointer and election flag without reclaiming the inherited runtime, while retaining the hook-installed flag. Initialization panic and ignored registration errors are limitations, not successful recovery paths. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:89-134)

## Error identity, classification and cloning

The full [error API/conversion matrix](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core-errors.md) is part of the core contract. An unknown commit outcome is Wrapped(CommitStatusUnknownError), keeping version and source while preserving the exhaustive Error enum. is_not_found explicitly vetoes that wrapper even if its source says a manifest was missing. Treating it as ordinary absence could drive a retry without establishing whether the first commit applied; the error itself instructs checking table state. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:94-127; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:748-761)

Not-found traversal is narrower than arbitrary source walking: direct NotFound, IO and Wrapped chains are recognized; an encountered Lance Error delegates to its own predicate and can stop traversal. Other typed accessors match direct variants/sources only. Thus maintaining an inspectable source chain does not automatically preserve top-level fence/backpressure/unknown-commit predicates. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:541-565; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:601-615; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:753-821)

Owned Arrow external and direct std IO boxed-Lance conversions attempt to recover the exact original Error. Borrowed Arrow and serde_json conversion stringify; Schema crosses Arrow through SchemaError and returns as Lance Arrow. DataFusion Context/Diagnostic wrappers are consumed, Collection keeps the first failure, and multi-owner Shared remains boxed External rather than recursively reclassified. Consumers modifying these mappings must preserve intended user-input categories and explicitly decide whether type/metadata loss is acceptable. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:843-955; rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:981-1039)

CloneableError selectively preserves not-found semantics, Timeout/IO categories, fence reason, backpressure and unknown-commit version. Its other cases become Cloned(text), including External; it does not promise retained original source types, locations or traces. CloneableResult derives cloning only for cloneable success T. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:1058-1147)

Field-not-found suggestions are computed only when formatting, but every candidate participates; the ten-name display cap does not bound search work. Distance counts Unicode scalars, threshold is floor(input scalar length/3), equal-distance ties preserve input option order, and exact short inputs can qualify. Changing any of these alters user-visible diagnostic text and potentially formatting cost. (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:57-88; rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:17-89)

## Field representation and tree operations

A Field is publicly mutable, but data_type() indexes required children and unwraps logical parsing. Fallible Arrow import checks only its explicit guards. Changes to child retention or logical grammar must preserve reconstructibility, or this apparently infallible accessor can panic. View types intentionally normalize, and reverse Arrow conversion does not restore field-ID metadata. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-195; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1204-1348; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:1531-1546)

Default comparison ignores dictionaries/metadata/field IDs; strict nullability remains checked. OneWay's expected/actual direction is expected || !actual. Two recognized logical blob forms compare only their shared prefix, so minimal-vs-complete can match while complete-vs-complete exposes range differences. Altering that distinction changes schema compatibility and diagnostics together. ### Raw values and fixed-size lists

ValueEncoder implements three distinct interfaces. Block compression accepts FixedWidth only and returns its unchanged buffer as Some, including empty buffers. Mini-block compression handles FixedWidth and nested FSL, with parallel validity buffers followed by the unchanged leaf buffer. Per-value compression handles FixedWidth or FSL; nullable FSL is copied into row-major validity bytes followed by leaf bytes, while nonnullable FSL moves its leaf storage. None of these paths performs IO. Invalid input handling differs: block/mini-block unsupported variants return errors, while per-value unsupported variants panic. Raw mini-block selection starts with two byte-aligned values, or eight nonaligned values using an estimated sixteen-value size. It doubles while estimated bytes remain strictly below 8186 and doubled count stays within the cached maximum. Initial count can already exceed a small configured maximum. Zero width reaches a debug assertion; malformed byte/count relationships are not validated. Full chunks retain a positive count log even when last; only a residual chunk gets log0. ### Variable-width interfaces and validation

Binary mini-blocks encode their own offset table at the beginning of each chunk, using signed32/64-bit input offsets rebased to chunk start plus table bytes. Each chunk is padded with0x48 to4/8-byte alignment respectively. The output is one concatenated buffer plus external chunk descriptors; logical num_values is retained from input even though chunk partitioning uses offsets.len()-1. Per-value VariableEncoder and VariableDecoder instead move an existing VariableWidthBlock unchanged. Whole-block VariableEncoder writes a separate width/data-start header, then original offsets and all original value bytes. These interfaces are not interchangeable. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:58-152; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:204-265; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:444-557)

The binary chunk target defaults4096 bytes via cached LANCE_BINARY_MINIBLOCK_CHUNK_SIZE; unparsable values fall back, parsed zero/negative values remain accepted. Chunk search starts at two values, grows by powers of two and treats final-tail fitting separately. The target is not a hard bound; alignment follows estimation, the initial two may exceed it, and the tail-fit branch bypasses MAX_MINIBLOCK_VALUES. The normal branch checks doubled candidate against the cap before accepting candidate, so cap4096 can stop at2048. new(Some(...)) still evaluates the lazy default because unwrap_or is eager. ### Byte-stream split and entropy

BSS groups each byte position across values in a single chunk: out[j*n+i]=in[i*width+j]. Width must be configured32/64; chunk caps are1024/512 values, independent of the configurable generic mini-block maximum. Final chunk has log0 even if full. Compression preserves total byte length and needs separate outer compression to save space. The encoder does not compare configured width to DataBlock width or validate physical size; short data panics, trailing data is ignored. Empty encode emits no buffers. Decode count0 returns before buffer validation; positive decode requires exactly one buffer and exact byte count, but does not know chunk maximum. Applying it to concatenated chunks uses the wrong transpose. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/byte_stream_split.rs:79-274)

Missing statistic returnsfalse, but completely empty BlockInfo registry panics in get_stat. Statistics sample the first min(num_values,64) rows, compute per-byte Shannon entropy and truncate entropy*1000 to integers. Missing physical bytes are skipped while sample-count denominator stays fixed. Selector does not verify statistic length/range or Arrow numeric type. The policy additionally requires a compression parameter present and not exactly none, even for BssMode::On; it does not itself validate that codec name in this helper. ### Packed struct representation and policy

Fixed packing transposes child buffers into row-major bytes. Mini-block packing reads DataSize and all children as FixedWidth, forwards the zipped block to raw ValueEncoder and stores field widths plus nested Flat metadata. Fixed per-value packing validates nonempty/equal-count/direct-fixed children, checked-sums widths and stores raw interleaved bytes. Fixed-size-list and nullable wrappers fail the direct FixedWidth test even if their logical type has fixed size. Mini decode assumes width consistency; fixed per-value decode explicitly checks byte alignment and child-width sum, but accepts surplus bytes and takes external count instead of input block.num_values. ComputeStat has no Result and GetStat can panic for uninitialized maps. Width cost uses entry_count*(value_bytes+length_bytes), with narrower widths winning ties; headers, child codecs and structural framing are excluded. ## V2 envelope and encoding layers

The minimal envelope permits independent item counts per column and stores byte buffers without imposing logical types. Data precedes column metadata, column metadata offset table, global buffer offset table, then the footer. Footer fields in order are three little-endian u64 offsets (column metadata start, column metadata table, global buffer table), two u32 counts (global buffers, columns), two u16 versions (major, minor), and LANC. The shared reader consumes exactly 40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-861). Padding may precede aligned buffers/metadata/table starts. Page buffers may be noncontiguous; 8 MB pages are advice, not a hard validity bound. (protos/file2.proto:11-115)

```text
file2 envelope
  data buffers
  column metadata blocks
    column encoding + optional column buffers
    pages: buffers + length + encoding + priority
  column metadata position/size table
  global buffer position/size table
  footer: A:u64 B:u64 C:u64 globals:u32 columns:u32 major:u16 minor:u16 LANC
```

The tree above reproduces the schema's composition: encoding locations are direct bytes, deferred byte range, or explicit none; page/column buffer offsets and sizes must have matching cardinality. Top-level row priority is distinct from a page's logical length. (protos/file2.proto:117-216)

The older lance.encodings namespace models Nullable/List/FixedSizeList and scalar transformations as ArrayEncoding, with ColumnEncoding wrappers for plain values, zone maps and blob descriptions. Its List encoding folds nullness into end offsets, but a strict greater-than null test in the comments conflicts with the formula at an equality boundary; see the [full analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_0.proto.md). This must be resolved from the decoder before implementing compatible list bytes. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:59-155; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:307-358)

The newer lance.encodings21 namespace separates structural layouts from compressive blocks. Layouts are MiniBlock, Constant, FullZip, Blob and Sparse; recursive compression alternatives include Flat, Variable, Constant, both bitpacking forms, FSST, Dictionary, RLE, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and both packed-struct forms. Exact fields and tag identities are in the [complete encoding analysis](../L2-files/protos/encodings_v2_1.proto.md). (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:341-357; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675)

```text

+-- global values buffer: concatenated child chunks
+-- global lengths buffer: concatenated child chunks
```

Stored coverage with no live coverage is **dormant**, distinct from a born-empty definition. Dormant stored vectors must be replaced, not merged back under stable row IDs. A deferred definition trains from saved parameters over the current column. Retrain/dormant rebuild checks exact expected coverage; definition-only degradation is accepted only when too-few-vector state is established and no files/coverage were produced. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:820-984; rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:1052-1190)

`num_indices_to_merge=Some(0)` appends a segment for unindexed rows without removing old ones; no unindexed rows makes that explicit append a no-op. The default can also append when existing segments are query-compatible but have different models, reusing the current suffix model. With no new rows, default optimize may rebalance. Ordinary merge selects a suffix, removes only segments actually merged, and derives metadata from those actual sources rather than an incompatible earlier segment. Preserve raw/provenance coverage and effective live coverage distinctions instead of replacing one with the other. (rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:1193-1437)

Concurrent changes are resolved at commit: CreateIndex/Rewrite ordering can withdraw coverage, preserve partial tagged provenance with scan fallback, or require a rebuild. A new segment's bitmap is a correctness assertion, not just a performance hint. Read the [directional conflict contract](protocol-commit.md#index-coverage-and-rewrite-lineage) before changing that assertion.

## Dataset ownership, version and mutation

A Dataset represents a checked-out manifest snapshot. `Dataset::open(uri)` loads through DatasetBuilder. Numeric checkout stays on the current branch; a named tag resolves its recorded branch/version. Checkout returns a new Dataset, while `checkout_latest(&mut self)` replaces manifest and derived fragment bitmap; it clears base-store caches if base paths changed. `main` is the default-branch alias in reference contexts. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:520-588)

Restore creates a **new** transaction based on the latest version, pointing at the currently checked-out historical version. It is not an in-place rewrite of that historical manifest. Detached commits do not become latest and do not join ordinary history; the builder also enforces existing-dataset/v2-manifest-path requirements. Public commit entry points accept operation/read version/store/handler/session parameters and delegate to the common path. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1459-1474; rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1620-1669; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-514)

Mutation methods have distinct handle effects: Rust builders commonly return a new Dataset/result; `&mut Dataset` convenience methods replace their state after success. Python native delete/update/restore/compaction/index methods replace the internal Arc after successful execution; an existing independently checked-out handle remains its own snapshot. Do not describe every Python method as returning a new Dataset: delete/update return count dictionaries, create_index returns the facade, and uncommitted index creation does not update the snapshot. (python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098; python/src/dataset.rs:2274-2288; python/src/dataset.rs:2867-2884; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:509-523; python/python/lance/dataset.py:4588-4619)

Storage mutation is not atomic merely because the public function returns Result: data files can exist before commit, and a storage error can follow successful publication. Use the [commit outcome contract](protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success) before retrying or cleaning files. Cleanup of old versions is separately destructive: removed versions cannot be checked out/restored and their unique data can be lost. The explanation path computes a cleanup plan without deleting files. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1477-1483; python/src/dataset.rs:2291-2338)

## Dataset open reference resolution

When a named branch is requested through an unmanaged store, DatasetBuilder marks checkout as delayed. Numeric-only version references remain relative to the URI chain. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:734-744)

For delayed checkout, the initial load_by_uri now receives None and loads the URI chain's latest version; it must not require the target branch's requested version number to exist on that initial chain. Non-delayed loading still passes the requested version number. This is a source-verified behavior change in the refresh. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:807-828)

After that initial load, delayed tag lookup resolves its branch/version on the loaded Dataset, and differing branch/version triggers checkout_version. The new initial-load rule preserves this later checkout stage rather than changing file-format gates or transaction conflict rules. (rust/lance/src/dataset/builder.rs:844-866)

[Ordered reference-open route](../L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md#dataset-open) · [Java mapped interface notes](../L1-modules/java.md#refresh-reference-based-opening-and-value-identity--mapped-only). Python declarations themselves did not change; its open/version family uses the shared DatasetBuilder boundary.

## Read/query contracts

Rust `Dataset::scan()` creates a Scanner. `try_into_stream` builds a physical plan and executes it; collecting batches is a separate operation. Plan order is source → filter → sort → limit/offset → late take/projection as required. Source selection and index use depend on search and prefilter options. Invalid combinations fail validation, and requesting projected constants alone is not automatically a supported row-count source. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2653-2696; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3246-3411)

`take` selects logical row positions; `take_rows` selects internal row IDs. IDs and encoded physical addresses are separate when stable IDs are enabled. Unfiltered count sums fragment counts; a filtered count uses a scanner with empty user projection plus row ID. Python's Arrow-expression count uses its scanner directly, whereas string/None count goes through the native Dataset count method. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1705-1778; python/python/lance/dataset.py:2616-2622; python/src/dataset.rs:1656-1685)

Python scanner defaults are applied before explicit non-None options. The final builder forwards options to the native scanner. Projection by names and projection by SQL transforms are mutually exclusive; string and Substrait filters are also mutually exclusive at the binding. Row-ID/address flags are separate; row-address prefilter bytes use the shared RowAddrMask decoder. FTS phrases cannot target multiple columns in the native dict-query route. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:1496-1565; python/python/lance/dataset.py:7361-7398; python/src/dataset.rs:1232-1437)

`LanceScanner.to_table` materializes the entire reader; `to_batches` iterates it. The native LanceReader owns a background stream producer, cancellation channel and bounded output channel. It terminates on first stream error/end or caller/channel cancellation; an unexpectedly closed producer channel becomes an error rather than silent EOF. Retaining all yielded batches can consume unbounded caller memory even though the channel is bounded. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:7412-7422; python/src/reader.rs:48-123)

DataFusion integration parses/qualifies identifiers according to planner options: exact field-name matching precedes ASCII case-insensitive matching; relation qualification is disabled by default and otherwise dots can represent nested access. The Dataset TableProvider translates projection/filter/limit into Scanner and declares Exact filter pushdown. Multiple output partitions are merged preserving known ordering, otherwise coalesced; a single partition executes directly. Preserve declared pushdown exactness when adding expressions. (rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350; rust/lance/src/datafusion/dataframe.rs:132-197; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)

`Dataset::write` accepts an iterator/stream conversion and InsertBuilder writes fragments before CommitBuilder publishes an Overwrite or Append operation. `execute_uncommitted` returns staged intent/data, not a visible new version. Python `write_dataset` validates/converts its input and destination, then native `_write_dataset` converts a native Scanner or Arrow stream and calls Rust Dataset::write. The binding recognizes case-insensitive create/append/overwrite and rejects other modes. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:202-315; python/python/lance/dataset.py:8363-8390; python/src/dataset.rs:4849-4888)

Python delete/update accept SQL or serialize Arrow expressions as Substrait. The native layer rejects predicates of other types, configures retry parameters, and delegates to DeleteBuilder/UpdateBuilder. Update assignments are strings parsed by the Rust builder; input/build errors map to ValueError and operation execution errors to IOError in this route. Returned keys are `num_deleted_rows` and `num_rows_updated`. The [conflict protocol](protocol-commit.md) determines whether operation recomputation is required. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:2938-2943; python/python/lance/dataset.py:3147-3158; python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098)

Python native index creation uppercases a supported high-level type discriminator. Generic `SCALAR` requires a config carrying its plugin type and serialized parameters, so custom plugin names need not be added as new built-in discriminators. Compaction has plan → execute tasks → commit phases for distributed use; the convenience execute path performs the whole operation and updates the Python handle.
